auditor.role: independent translation auditor (team lopdev); not the translator, not the draft auditor, not the integrator
auditor.independence: I translated, audited and integrated none of this programme's ru work: I read the English, the sidecar and the landed bytes myself and re-derived every structural claim here rather than adopting the earlier records, which I only used to decide which two NITs to re-test.

findings.note: «Отменить проверку» is the first time «проверка» becomes a control label. In the shipped ru corpus the word carries the check/verification/checking sense ~75 times across ~30 files («Проверка обновлений», «Ожидает проверки», «На проверке»), while 'check-in' has exactly one prose precedent: ui.chat.run_details.wake.managed_note «Чтобы остановить эти проверки…». No text change: the paired title «Отменить проверку ассистента {name}?» disambiguates it, the destructive/Keep pair makes the act unambiguous, and English itself spends two words on one object ('check-in' in title+button, 'wake' in the body). Action: record check-in → проверка in the ru term ledger so the next translator does not re-decide it, and so a future button outside this dialog does not silently reuse «проверка» for the other sense.

Width: «Отменить пробуждение» is 20 chars against English 'Cancel wake' at 11 (1.82x, where the ru style guide plans for +20-30%); the sibling «Отменить проверку» is 17 against 'Cancel check-in' at 15 (1.13x, fine). No text change recommended: it is byte-identical to the two shipped corpus strings for the same English (ui.chat.run_details.wake.cancel_wake, ui.schedules.wake_conversation_row.cancel_wake), and the confirm row (wake-cancel-popover.tsx) is a flex row of intrinsically sized size="sm" buttons with no truncation class, so nothing clips — the card only grows. Flagged for a rendered check of the popover and the Schedules confirm dialog at their minimum width: I did not render pixels, so the growth is reasoned from the markup, not observed.

binding: Hashes verified FIRST, all matching the brief: HEAD 90f0f49beae27ad35c1b05492ee150cd31e3a8c1; ru file b2c5993276ae0776469d547b476579dd98238b7035836cf05cdea11bd6e7e900; en c5c484fbc04cc433dce666123e233ae83ac5d03d8e9274a7945b83ec419612fa; context fe162255233a62a41add06ce77e0aff3a533c003e3fb9e504031b91aa83073de; audited draft ru.v2.json b2c5993276ae0776469d547b476579dd98238b7035836cf05cdea11bd6e7e900. The landed file is byte-identical to that draft (cmp exit 0). Key budget: 12 keys, identical key set and identical order to English (set difference empty both ways). Format: TAB indent on every value line, no double indent, no trailing whitespace, exactly one trailing newline, no BOM, no CRLF or lone CR, NFC-normalised, no \u escapes. ICU: parsed every value with the repo's own @formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser 3.5.21 (the module scripts/i18n/locale-parity.test.mjs uses); argument names and select arms are identical to English for all 12 keys — {name} on title_named; {subject}+{head} with subject arms head/other on message; {subject}+{head}+{name} with subject arms head/other on message_named; no arguments elsewhere. No plural or selectordinal exists in English or ru, so no extra ru categories (one/few/many/other) are required by this namespace. Rendered with intl-messageformat 12.1.3 at locale ru for every arm and both name shapes (Atlas, Research agent), and both arms produce complete, well-formed sentences. English sweep: literal-node extraction proves zero Latin letters and zero digits in visible text — the only Latin in the file is ICU syntax (subject/select/head/other/name), which never renders. Bidi: no bidi control characters and no zero-width/BOM/NBSP characters in any value; ru is 'ltr' per i18n/languages.json, so RTL placement does not apply and the embedded Latin tokens are ICU names only. Every value read and judged against English and the sidecar; both NITs above are ones I independently re-confirmed against the corpus. I did not render UI pixels, ran no tsc/build/test suite, and edited nothing.
